newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends unchanged despite stock falls.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends unchanged despite stock falls.

text.p: Key September three-month Euroyen interest rate futures closed unchanged on Thursday.

Despite continued falls in Tokyo stocks, the key contract failed to rally as profit-taking was waiting at above 99.30, traders said. The contract settled unchanged at 99.30 after moving between 99.28 and 99.31. Turnover was 47,825 contracts.
"Euroyen futures could have been bought given weak stocks and strong yen bonds," said a city bank dealer.
"But what happened today was that people were busy with fixing their profits as the market was approaching its short-term ceiling," he said.

The key September contract's life-time high was 99.33 and traders said it may face difficulties rising beyond that level unless the Bank of Japan starts guiding money market rates below current levels.
"It is obvious that even if stocks fall further, the monetary authorities cannot do anything for the time being.
They should wait until financial institutions close their books at the end of March," the city bank dealer said.
The Nikkei 225 closed Thursday down 3.25 percent, or 606.51 points, at 18,073.87. The index has lost 1,287.48 points in the first four trading days of 1997.

Meanwhile, Japanese government bond (JGB) cash and futures markets rallied for the third business day on Thursday, fuelled by expectations for good auction results of 10-year JGBs even with a record low 2.7 percent coupon rate.

Key March JGB futures rose to 125.26 before ending up 0.15 at 124.95. The auction produced a lowest price of 100.50, which was much higher than expected, and this dampened investors' appetite for the bonds because they cannot buy them under par.
Given the central bank's neutral money market operation this morning, cash money market rates were little changed, traders said.

The key interbank overnight call rate was mainly traded at 0.48 percent against Wednesday's 0.49. The long-end benchmark three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.53 percent, unchanged from Wednesday's issued rate. The issued volume was some 150 billion yen.
Neither one- nor two-month CDs were issued, but were offered at 0.50 and 0.51 percent, respectively, traders said. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk (81-33432-8570)
